messages:
sarah-sales: Quick thread—Fenix (enterprise search) wants a custom Dedicated commit proposal. They want: 2x A100 reserved pool (24/7), autoscale burst credits for spikes, and a 12-month term. Asking for a 15% commit discount + ability to roll unused burst credits month->month. Quote linked: https://redwood/quote/FX-2034 :eyes:
omar-gtm: Thanks — can you drop the numbers (baseline RUs, expected spikes) and the business justification? We should loop in revops/finance for the discount. Also will they need on-prem networking?
tess-revops: Copying numbers from the call. Baseline: 600k token-min/day steady. Peak: bursts up to 6x baseline 4–6x/day for ~15m. Proposed commercial model (draft):
```
Baseline reserved: 2 x A100 pool (24/7) — $XX,XXX/month
Autoscale burst credits: prepaid bucket 500 GPU-min/mo (rollover allowed up to 3 months)
Overage: $Y per GPU-min beyond bucket
Commit discount: 15% on baseline for 12-mo term; 7% on autoscale bucket
Condition: discount capped if sustained average >4x baseline for 60 days
```
diego-legal: Need to flag the "rollover" language. We prefer capped rollover (max 3 months) and a clause that we can audit usage for misuse. Also remove auto-renew for the prepaid burst credits; make explicit PO required. Add standard indemnity and data handling bullets.
kai-eng: From infra side — the burst path has a warmup of ~60s for cold vGPU allocation; sustained sub-15m spikes will be fine, but 4–6x bursts might cause throttling at scale unless we reserve a small warm pool. If we add a 10% always-warm headroom it'll reduce effective burst consumption but costs rise. Suggest we offer a technical option: "warm pool" (adds 0.2 x baseline cost) or purely on-demand (better unit cost but higher latency).
autoscale-bot: Provisioning estimate for FX-2034 request:
- Warm pool option: reserve 0.2 x baseline (est 0.4 A100) — provisioning +5 mins
- Pure burst (on-demand): cold start ~60–90s, 95th pct concurrency risk if many customers burst simultaneously
- Estimated monthly GPU-min for 6x spikes (15m, 4/day): ~7200 GPU-min/month

sarah-sales: Thanks — we should present two commercial alternatives to the customer: (A) Baseline + warm pool + smaller prepaid burst bucket (lower latency, slightly higher baseline spend), (B) Baseline + larger prepaid burst bucket (cheaper baseline, more prepaid credits, longer rollovers). Which one can we price aggressively to win the POC?
tess-revops: I can stretch to 18% on baseline for a 12-mo locked commit if finance signs off and legal accepts capped rollover + audit clause. For warm pool option add 6% uplift to baseline cost. Will prep two redlines and a clean quote.
diego-legal: Fine with capped 3-month rollover + audit + PO-only refill. Remove "auto fallback to older models" clause in SLA. Need security questionnaire answer pack before we send the final.
maria-finance: From finance: provisional approval for up to 18% discount on baseline for 12-mo if ARR qualifies (>$250k ARR) and we secure net-30 PO. Any deeper discounts need CRO sign-off. Please include revenue recognition notes in the SOW.
sarah-sales: Great. Can someone assemble a single doc with: final price table, SLA redline, security QA pack, and a one-pager commercial summary I can send to the buyer by EOD tomorrow? I’ll attach the customer POC acceptance criteria. :thumbsup:
omar-gtm: I'll coordinate the slide one-pager and distill the exec justification. cc @tess-revops for the exact numbers and @diego-legal for the redline.
tess-revops: On it — will upload the two quote options and redline to the deal folder: https://redwood/deals/FX-2034/quote-drafts by EOD.
sarah-sales: Requesting deal desk provisional approval to offer option A with 18% baseline discount + warm pool (6% uplift) and 3-month capped rollover on burst credits. Approver: finance + legal sign-off required.
maria-finance: Provisionally approved (margins checked) pending signed PO and SOW language on revenue recognition.
diego-legal: Approved conditional on the SLA redline and the security questionnaire answers included in the package.
sarah-sales: Perfect — I'll send the customer the two options and flag the warm-pool recommendation for their latency-sensitive queries. Will update here after the customer reply. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
